description: A Lean 4 + Mathlib library of machine-checked uniform oscillatory-integral estimates with explicit constants: van der Corput's lemma for every derivative order, and the second-derivative bound with its sharp constant; non-stationary and nondegenerate stationary phase; uniform decay at fold (A2), cusp (A3) and umbilic (D4) points with the D4 leading term and its closed-form constant (also uniformly over totally bounded families of C² amplitudes and over bounded linear terms); global decay from a pointwise classification of the phase (also for amplitudes in any complex Banach space); front ends in Mathlib's idiom; and explicit bounds for the propagator kernel of the free discrete Schrödinger equation: on Z, |∫_{-π}^{π} e^{i(t cos k + ξk)} dk| ≤ 8(1 + √7)/3 · t^{-1/3} for all t > 0 and real ξ, and on Z^d the d-th power of that constant with t^{-d/3}. For the same equation the library proves, on ℓ²(Z^d), existence and uniqueness of solutions, their kernel representation and ℓ¹ → ℓ^∞ decay (1 + |t|)^{-d/3} with an explicit constant, and, on a ring of N sites and on an open chain, the propagator with explicit finite-size bounds against the infinite line. It also contains the Hadamard quantum walk on the line with an explicit t^{-1/3} dispersive bound, the exponentially convergent trapezoidal rule for periodic functions analytic in a strip with the Fourier-coefficient bound behind it, and the Kusmin–Landau inequality for exponential sums in Landau's sharp form. The degenerate-point and global bounds are uniform over all linear terms of the phase, as dispersive estimates need. Statements are frozen, timestamped and reviewed blind before their Lean proofs (exceptions are disclosed), and the proofs are replayed by six kernel checkers; a downstream checker verifies that a project depends on exactly the reviewed statements. Proofs and reviews are largely by AI agents; statement fidelity has been reviewed by AI referees, among them one of a different model family, not yet by a human expert.
